thread:
maya: Thinking out loud — we should add a 'model credits' window for per-model families so customers can have different burst envelopes for small vs large models. Proposal: per-org + per-key credit buckets, with size-weighted burn (e.g., 1 token on 7B = 1 credit, 1 token on 70B = 4 credits). Soft-burst window = 60s, refill rate = sustained qps budget. Want thoughts on fairness + console UX.
dan: +1 on weighting. main concern is routing complexity — if a key exhausts credits for a model family, do we block, fallback to cheaper variant, or queue?
maya: Thinking fallback to compatible smaller family first, then queue, then 429 if none. Fallback policy configurable per org in console.
serena: Telemetry-wise we need both credit burn and effective latency cost. Suggest exposing metrics: `credits_used_per_minute`, `fallback_rate_by_model_family`, `avg_tokens_per_call_by_family`. Those let us tune weights.
kai: Implementation nit: prefer token-seconds accounting instead of flat multiplier to account for seq length. Eg: credits = tokens * weight * (avg_latency_ms / 100). That penalizes long context on big models.
dan: That seems reasonable but increases compute to compute credits per request at edge. We need a cheap approximation for fast path. Maybe precompute weight*expected_seq_scale per model and update periodically.
maya: Console UX idea: show a waterfall per family: allocated monthly credits, sustained qps, recent burst usage. Allow ops to set "burst reserve" for emergencies and a one-click temporary override (with audit log).
serena: +1 on audit log. Also add alerts: time-to-drain for current credits and predicted overage. We can feed into existing cost alerts.
kai: For enforcement, I'd do a three-tier check at request ingress: 1) fast local cache token budget check, 2) central quota service for reconciliation asynchronously, 3) fallback decision. That preserves low latency.
dan: How about fairness across orgs if they share Dedicated capacity? Need reservable capacity vs shared pool. Credits could map to capacity tokens that the scheduler consumes. If shared pool low, we automatically reduce per-key burst allowance.
maya: Good point. For Dedicated we should surface a tenant-level 'dedicated-burst-multiplier' that gates all model families. For hosted API, default is shared-pool fallback.
ops-bot: PR opened: <https://git.internal/repo/pull/4823> — initial credit algorithm + console mockups. Tagging @maya @kai for review.
maya: Thanks — will review. Next up: sketch API changes — probably add `X-Model-Credit-Burn` header in responses and an admin endpoint `/quota/status?key=...` for live preview. Thoughts?
dan: `X-Model-Credit-Burn` is useful for customers. Also include `x-fallback-used` boolean when we downgrade model.
serena: We should keep header sizes minimal but include numeric credit delta and family name. Eg `X-Model-Credit: gpt-70b=12`.
kai: For testing, let's synthetic-run burst scenarios against routing to ensure we don't introduce head-of-line blocking. I can set up a harness.
maya: Great — I'll post the console mock and sample API in the PR comments. If everyone is cool, we'll aim for a canary rollout on staging next week. :thumbsup:
